newsitem.title: USA: Wis. governor proposes $200 mln environmental plan.
newsitem.headline: Wis. governor proposes $200 mln environmental plan.

text.p: Wisconsin Gov. Tommy Thompson on Monday announced a $200 million, partly bond-financed environmental program.

The Republican governor said his plan, which will be part of the $36 billion fiscal 1998 budget he is scheduled to unveil Wednesday, will encourage the clean up of contaminated, so-called brownfield sites, improve drinking water, renew the state's committment to forests and wildlife and reshape the relationship of business and state regulatory agencies.
According to the state's budget office, the plan would include about $50 million of general obligation bonds for the safe drinking water portion.

The only other new proposal in Thompson's budget for the fiscal year that begins July 1 that calls for bonding is a five-year, $500 million plan called TEACH (Technology for Educational Achievement in Wisconsin).
The program, which calls for $50 million in annual GO bonding, would bring computer hardware, software and training to schools.
